alkylation reagent: Protein alkylation was performed with 0.05 M iodoacetamide in an urea buffer for 20 min at RT.
alkylation concentration: Protein alkylation was performed with 0.05 M iodoacetamide in an urea buffer for 20 min at RT.
cleavage agent: Finally, trypsinization of proteins (trypsin ratio 1:100, Sigma-Aldrich, Darmstadt, Germany), centrifugation at 16,000 g for 10 min, and lyophilization were performed.
collision energy: Normalized collision energy was set to 33 and the precursor ions were excluded for final activation (45 s, 5 ppm mass tolerance).
fragmentation method: Top 10 precursor ions between m/z ratio 300 and 2200, intensity threshold 500 counts, and FT mass resolution of 60,000, were subjected in a higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) fragmentation.
instrument: The proteomic analysis of all samples was performed using LC/MS on the Dionex Ultimate 3000 UHPLC system coupled with the high resolution nano-ESI Orbitrap-Elite mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific).
ionization type: Positive ion electrospray ionization was applied in order to achieve the gaseous exchange transition of the peptides.
labeling: The proteomic analysis of all samples was performed using LC/MS on the Dionex Ultimate 3000 UHPLC system coupled with the high resolution nano-ESI Orbitrap-Elite mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific).
reduction reagent: A sample reduction with 10 mM DTE for 20 min at room temperature (RT), was performed.
reduction concentration: A sample reduction with 10 mM DTE for 20 min at room temperature (RT), was performed.
